q: The Liouville-Arnold theorem on integrability requires the first integrals F₁,…,Fₙ to be in involution. This means:
opts: {Fᵢ, Fⱼ} = δᵢⱼ (Kronecker delta) for the Poisson bracket
{Fᵢ, Fⱼ} = 0 for all i,j (pairwise vanishing Poisson brackets)
The Hamiltonian flows of Fᵢ and Fⱼ commute only at t=0
exp: In involution means {Fᵢ,Fⱼ} = 0 for all i,j. This ensures the Hamiltonian flows of each Fᵢ commute, allowing simultaneous canonical coordinates (action-angle). It is the condition for Liouville integrability.
